In Japan, national health insurance covers orthodontic treatment for children with malocclusions caused by a specific list of 66 diseases designated by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), primarily consisting of congenital anomalies that affect jaw growth, oral function, and occlusion, as established under the 2024 insurance revisions.

This coverage applies to pediatric cases where the malocclusion is directly attributable to one of these designated conditions, with treatment restricted to MHLW-approved facilities that meet strict criteria for equipment, personnel, and expertise.

Beyond the 66 diseases, limited additional coverage exists for cases involving eruption failure of three or more permanent teeth (under specific surgical criteria) and pre- and post-surgical orthodontics for jaw deformities requiring operative correction.

The national health insurance coverage for pediatric orthodontic treatment in Japan primarily targets malocclusions caused by congenital anomalies that affect jaw and oral function, with a focus on pediatric patients to enable early intervention during growth and development.
This coverage aims to improve functional impairments, including chewing efficiency (咀嚼機能), speech articulation (言語機能), and overall oral function, rather than addressing purely aesthetic concerns.

Coverage extends to malocclusions linked to 66 designated diseases specified by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, as well as limited additional cases such as non-eruption of three or more permanent teeth or pre- and post-surgical orthodontics for jaw deformities (detailed in respective sections).
Treatment is restricted to approved facilities meeting MHLW standards to ensure quality and appropriateness.

Coverage expanded in 1990 to include pre- and post-surgical orthodontics for jaw deformities (顎変形症) requiring surgical intervention. In 2002, it further broadened to encompass six additional diseases designated by the Minister of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), establishing the framework of linking insurance eligibility to specific congenital conditions.

The 2024 (Reiwa 6) medical fee revisions, as outlined by the MHLW, added five more conditions—Klippel-Feil syndrome (congenital cervical spine fusion), Alagille syndrome, high IgE syndrome, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, and Gardner syndrome—confirming the current list of 66 designated diseases, primarily congenital anomalies affecting jaw and oral function.
Primary Coverage for Designated Diseases

In Japan, national health insurance provides primary coverage for pediatric orthodontic treatment targeting malocclusions directly caused by 66 specific diseases designated by the Minister of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW).

These diseases are predominantly congenital anomalies affecting the development and function of the jaw and oral region, resulting in bite abnormalities that impair essential functions such as mastication, speech, and swallowing.

Coverage applies specifically to orthodontic interventions that address these disease-linked malocclusions, such as open bite, mandibular prognathism, facial asymmetry, and crowding, to restore functional occlusion and support growth-related oral health needs.

As of the 2024 revisions, the list comprises 66 such conditions, emphasizing those with clear causal links to malocclusions that necessitate early and ongoing orthodontic management, often starting in childhood to optimize outcomes during developmental stages.

Insurance coverage under this primary provision is restricted to treatment performed at MHLW-approved facilities that meet specific criteria and are registered with local health authorities, ensuring standardized care and appropriate multidisciplinary approaches where needed.

In addition to orthodontic coverage for malocclusions arising from the 66 designated diseases, Japan's national health insurance provides limited coverage for two other categories of cases involving pediatric patients.

One category involves malocclusions caused by failure of eruption of three or more permanent anterior teeth and premolars (前歯及び小臼歯の永久歯のうち3歯以上の萌出不全), restricted to cases requiring fenestration surgery (埋伏歯開窓術) for impacted teeth. This provision addresses severe impaction-related occlusal issues where surgical exposure is necessary to enable orthodontic intervention.

The other category covers pre- and post-surgical orthodontic treatment for jaw deformities (顎変形症), limited to cases necessitating surgery such as jaw osteotomy (顎離断等の手術を必要とするもの). This applies to skeletal discrepancies requiring orthognathic surgery, with insurance supporting orthodontic phases immediately before and after the procedure to correct associated malocclusions.

These additional provisions are distinct from disease-based coverage and, like all insured orthodontic treatments, require performance at facilities that meet MHLW facility standards and have submitted notifications to the local health bureau.

These institutions qualify as insurance medical institutions for specific billing categories, such as those designated for the orthodontic diagnosis fee ("矯診") applicable to malocclusions caused by designated diseases or eruption failure, or the jaw and oral function diagnosis fee ("顎診") for pre- and post-surgical orthodontics related to jaw deformities.

To achieve designation, facilities must comply with MHLW criteria concerning equipment, staffing, and operational capabilities, then formally notify their local Health and Welfare Bureau (or Branch Bureau), which maintains and publishes the resulting lists of approved institutions.
